producer_report.summary:
The gate now lands a squash that closes several jobs when their athena.candidate/2 records form one valid chain, and still refuses every broken variant. A single-job landing is judged exactly as before. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are clean. The athena-gate suite (67 tests) and the xtask policy test pass after the final doc edit. The full `cargo test --locked` passed before the doc edits. I did not re-run it afterwards: the doc edits touch only docs/, and the xtask policy test, which reads docs/enforcement.md, passes.

**Gate (invariant.rs)**
- `landing` is split into the chain check (`chain_problem`) and the per-job checks (`job_problem`). `job_problem` is the old single-job body. For one job it still requires the landed content, with the same messages.
- For two or more jobs the chain check runs first, then every job goes through `job_problem`. Only the last job must hold the landed content. Earlier jobs must have candidate.fingerprint equal to verified_fingerprint.
- The chain check follows design §4.2 and uses the §4.3 messages. It covers:
  - a /1 candidate in a chain;
  - a commit with more than one parent;
  - a job that changes a .gitattributes, either in its recorded changes or in the commit diff;
  - a fork;
  - an unlinked job, a missing middle job or a cycle;
  - no head, or a wrong head base;
  - a broken fingerprint link;
  - a last job that does not hold the tree.
- A chain's head is a job with no previous_job, or one whose predecessor landed on the parent. The predecessor can be a /1 record. One job left from a partly landed chain uses the single-job rule.
- `landing_job` now returns a set of jobs. `jobs::check` accepts a landed outcome if its job is in that set. The history walk records every job of a chain.
- The `Athena-Job` trailer must now name a job the commit lands. The old message is kept for a single job.

**Tests**
- landing_tests.rs holds the hand-built two-job chain and the three-job chain. Repeated fingerprints are covered: a job that reverts an earlier one, and a job that changes nothing.
- It also holds the refusal tests from criteria 2 and 3: the partly landed cases, the two-parent merge, and one test that fails each per-job check on a middle job.
- jobs.rs has two tests: every outcome of a chain is accepted, and a broken chain's outcomes are refused. history.rs has one: repeating a middle job after a chain landed is refused by the history walk.
- Existing landing tests are unchanged.

**Docs**
- enforcement.md has a new row M30, and the M23 row gains two chain tests. The "refused today" paragraph is replaced.
- D69 is marked accepted and implemented. The design's status note lists where the build differs from the text. v0 §7.3, architecture.md, records.md and the CHANGELOG are updated.
- I did not touch crates/athena-gate/src/lib.rs or crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs. They needed no change: `landing_tests` is already visible crate-wide, and `RecordSet::load` already reads /2. No governance file or records/ path changed.

checks_run.note: Full workspace run was green before the doc edits. Afterwards I re-ran only `cargo test --locked -p xtask -p athena-gate` and the xtask policy test.
After the doc edits the enforcement-map test failed once because a backticked `previous_job` in the M30 row was read as a test name. I removed the backticks and the policy test passes.

open_issues: A chain whose net content equals the parent's (for example A to B, then B to A) is not a chain landing. Its fingerprint matches the parent's, so `check` takes the records-only path and wants a trailer. This is not tested and was not in scope.
The design's previous_job derivation tests (§5 item 4, last entries) live in athena-core's chain.rs, not the gate. I did not check that they cover every case listed.

The design's "merge commit whose first-parent diff adds several jobs" test asserts the message `check` shows, as asked. The merge-path text of the §4.3 refusal is still not passed through, which is out of scope.
The D69 decision text still says the implementation is a follow-up job. I left it as the original wording and added a status line above it saying it is implemented.
mistakes: My first no-head test made job 1 follow job 2, which also forked job 3, so it hit the fork message. I changed it to a circle of all three jobs.
learnings: AnyRecord::parse refuses a /1 candidate that carries chain fields and a /2 without base_fingerprint. So a loaded candidate with base_fingerprint set is a /2, and JobFiles did not need to record the schema version.
xtask's `every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists` treats every backticked token in docs/enforcement.md rows as a test name. Field names and code identifiers must not be backticked there.
`mod landing_tests` is a private module at the gate crate root, so sibling modules (jobs.rs, history.rs) can use its `pub(crate)` helpers with no lib.rs change.
`check` calls `landing` for a merge commit only when the merge's content equals neither parent's. A chain squash merged that way shows the generic merge message, as design §4.6 says.
desires: A way to run the single test file or an xtask policy check before writing docs rows, so I would not learn that backticks are read as test names only from a failure.
